Here you can appoint any one of the currently running agents as the commander (you can switch at any time, even mid-work). When the commander writes `@target: instruction` (`@all:` for everyone), it reaches you as a **📮 notification**. Nothing is ever typed into any agent's input box automatically — you decide whether to actually relay the instruction (via the Cockpit broadcast or by typing into a terminal yourself). cockpit.commander_and_watchdog_help: The deterministic watchdog (detecting stalls, loops, and error bursts) runs regardless of this setting, and reports anomalies here and in notifications. Here you can name any one of the currently running agents as the “commander” (you can swap it at any time, even mid-task). When the commander writes `@target: instruction` (`@all:` for everyone), that text reaches the user as a **📮 notification**. It is never written automatically into any agent's input box — you decide whether the instruction is actually sent (via Cockpit's broadcast or by typing into each terminal). It also never sends destructive operations such as stop or restart to agents on its own. The named agent can still be used for ordinary work, and that session is itself watched too.

coedit.cli_help:
zai coedit — zero-conflict proof (measured proof that the later merge lands in one shot)

      zai coedit proof   [--repo <dir>] [--base <ref>] [--band <n>] [--json] [<branch>...]
      zai coedit merge   [--repo <dir>] [--base <ref>] [--band <n>] [--json] [--dry-run] [--force] [<branch>...]
      zai coedit regions [--repo <dir>] [--base <ref>] [--json] <branch>

      With no branch given, every branch ahead of the merge target is used
      (branches held by another worktree are excluded).

      --band <n>   Safety band, in lines (default 1). The default 1 is the measured floor
                   for three-way merges; going lower breaks the one-shot merge guarantee.
                   Specify 3 if patch application (git apply / git am) must pass too.
      --force      Merge even without a proof, as long as the dry run is clean
                   (such a merge carries no “one-shot” guarantee).

    Exit codes:
      0  Proof holds / every branch merged
      1  Proof failed / merge stopped (no ref was moved)
      2  Argument error, or the repository cannot be read
      3  git is too old for the dry run (downgraded to proof only; no ref was moved)

guard.commit_blocked_line_ownership:
Commit blocked (Zaivern Code line-range ownership).
The changes you staged touch lines held by another owner:

{list}
When two people touch the same lines, the conflict stays invisible until the merge.
(Inside one file you can still write at the same time if you stay {band} lines apart. Only the overlap is blocked)
What to do:
  (1) Wait for the other side to finish, then commit again
  (2) Split the work — take a different line range / file / directory
  (3) Take it over: check with `zai lease list`, then free it with `zai lease release --agent <name>`
  (4) Let just this commit through: `git commit --no-verify` (the conflict stays)
  (5) Remove the guard: `zai guard uninstall`
guard.git_is_the_checkpoint: Whatever the agent, whatever the editor, results have to go through git. We put a checkpoint right there, so commits touching files owned by someone else can be stopped without waiting for any vendor.

guard.write_blocked_symlink_escapes_repo:
Write blocked (Zaivern Code guard).
{rel} is spelled as if it were inside the repository, but it goes through a symlink
and points **outside the repository**.

git never puts this path into the index (`beyond a symbolic link`), so the
commit-time guard will never see it. If the link lands in another worktree,
that place belongs to someone sharing the same ledger.
What to do:
  (1) Skip the link and write using the real path directly
  (2) If writing outside the repository really is fine, use an absolute path outside the repository
guard.write_blocked_unresolvable_symlink:
Write blocked (Zaivern Code guard).
The symlink at {rel} could not be resolved (it loops, or it cannot be read).
**Anything whose target file is unknown does not get through.**
Fix: repair the link, or write using the real path directly
guard.zai_lacks_guard_subcommand:
This zai does not accept the `zai guard` subcommand yet.
If you install it anyway, every commit will launch the editor and the hook will never return.
Fix: update to a zai that has it merged, then run `zai guard init` again

negotiate.cli_help:
zai negotiate — when line regions collide, shift instead of refusing

  zai negotiate offer      < in.json   Propose an answer to one request
  zai negotiate allocate   < in.json   Hand out N requests as disjoint regions
  zai negotiate deal       < in.json   Reply to a batch of negotiation messages
  zai negotiate serve                  Actually act as the negotiator on the mesh
                                       [--rounds N] [--lines N] [--band N]
  zai negotiate ask --spec <region>    Ask the negotiator for a region and wait
                                       [--movable] [--size-only] [--to <pid>]
                                       [--as <pid>] [--rounds N] [--max-shift N]
  zai negotiate help                   This usage

Input is JSON on stdin. A region is written as the spec string "src/a.rs#L10-40".

  offer:    {"file_lines":2000,"band":3,
             "want":{"id":"t1","region":"src/a.rs#L10-40","movable":true},
             "occupied":[{"holder":"bob","region":"src/a.rs#L1-50","until":0}]}
  allocate: Same shape, with "wants":[...] instead of "want"
  deal:     Same shape, with "inbox":["<one-line Deal>", ...] and "me":"your own name"

Only `--movable` states that shifting is allowed. Without it the region is
**never shifted** — a region is bound to the *content that is there*, not to line
numbers, so shifting it unasked means telling someone to edit a different function.

Exit codes:
  0  Fits as is / all were handed out / acquired (ask)
  1  Cannot fit at all / none were handed out / refused (ask)
  2  Usage error (input unreadable, unknown subcommand)
  3  There is a proposal (shift, split, wait) / only some were handed out
     For serve/ask, the "exactly one negotiator" rule was broken
     (serve = one is already there / ask = none is there)
  4  Waited to the limit but no reply came (ask only; different from being refused)
  5  The mesh is disabled (run `zai mesh join` first)

tutorial.acp_body:
Instead of reading characters off the screen, this is a channel where the agent reports its own state.
With an agent that supports it, stalls and pending approvals stop being guesswork.
tutorial.acp_structured_protocol: ACP — Connect via a Structured Protocol
tutorial.add_terminals_body:
Aside from agents, you can open as many plain shells as you need.
Opening and closing the panel itself is a keystroke away.
tutorial.agent_cockpit_body:
Every running agent lines up in a grid of live terminals, and the input box on top sends to all of them at once.
A watcher detects stalls, loops and abnormal exits and raises them to you (it never types on its own).
With 💡 Super Agent you can also appoint one of them as the commander.
tutorial.append_only_changes_never_confl: Stop Append-Only Changes, Like Adding to a List, From Conflicting
tutorial.approval_queue_body:
Every agent's pending approvals gather into a single queue where you allow or deny them.
Each decision is recorded in the audit log, so you can trace later who approved what.
tutorial.assignment_table_that_cannot_co: Build an assignment table that cannot collide, before you hand the work out
tutorial.auto_release_dead_owner_claims: Automatically Release Ownership Still Held by a Dead Assignee
tutorial.back_and_forward_navigation:
You can jump somewhere and come straight back to where you were.
It feels just like moving back and forth in a browser.
tutorial.board_body:
Get an overview of every agent across 8 lanes: Idle / Thinking / Editing / Running / Verifying / Awaiting approval / Stalled / Done.
In vertical mode, selecting a card opens a live terminal below it; move with ↑↓ and type straight in with Enter.
Estimates are marked ≈, and solid evidence is marked ✓.
tutorial.bookmarks_body:
Mark any line that catches your eye and jump back to it from the list at any time.
Add a mnemonic and you can recall it with a single character.
tutorial.builtin_agent_catalog:
A built-in catalog recognizes 29 CLI agents (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor and more).
Add as many presets as you like under [[agents]] in config.toml, and separate accounts with env.
tutorial.bundled_plugins_body:
worktrees, diff-review, tasks, quick-actions and more ship by default and are active from the first launch.
They are plain shell scripts, so you can read them, copy them and rewrite them (no Rust rebuild needed).
You can also export / install them as .zvplug.
tutorial.changes_gutter_review_github: Change List, Gutter, Diff Review, GitHub
tutorial.check_conflict_protection: Check how well you are protected from conflicts right now
tutorial.code_folding_body:
Fold by indentation structure, and unfold everything at once.
Use it to grasp the shape of a long file.
tutorial.command_palette_body:
One input box spans files, commands, agents and worktrees.
No prefix = files, > = commands, @ = agents, # = git worktrees.
tutorial.completion_format_rename_body:
Once a language server is connected, you get completion, find references, rename, formatting and quick fixes.
Format on save is toggled from the command palette.
tutorial.edit_lines_body:
Toggle line comments, duplicate a line, and move lines up or down — all from the keyboard.
Undo / redo is independent for each tab.
tutorial.editor_basics_body:
syntect syntax highlighting, a line-number gutter, and an unsaved marker (●).
The gutter is colored by git changes (green = added / yellow = modified) and LSP diagnostics (red / yellow).
tutorial.fanout_race_body:
Send a single instruction to 2-4 agents at once, each running in its own git worktree.
Conflicting files are compared while they run: merge the ones you adopt, and discard the rest by deleting the whole worktree so no leftovers remain.
tutorial.file_tree_and_git_colors_body:
Changed files get an M / A / U / D / R / C badge, and the color carries up to collapsed parent folders.
Right-click for new, rename, delete, and Send @path to Agent.
Switching tabs makes the tree follow along automatically.
tutorial.filter_features: Filter by name, description or keystroke
tutorial.find_in_file_body:
It shows the hit count while jumping each matching line to the center of the screen.
When an agent terminal has focus, it searches the entire scrollback instead.
tutorial.find_search_palette_bookmarks: Find in File, Search Across Files, Palette, Bookmarks
tutorial.find_semantic_conflicts: Find Changes That Clash Across Different Files
tutorial.finish_body:
Now just let it run. For a full feature index and chapter-by-chapter reading, open the Full Feature Guide below (Help > Restart Tutorial brings you back here).
Have a good night.
tutorial.follow_an_agent_body:
The view moves automatically to whichever agent just produced output; turn it off and it stays put.
If you lose track, you can resume following.
tutorial.git_panel_body:
List changed files, stage, commit and work with branches from here.
git status is refreshed every 2 seconds on a background thread, so frames never drop even in a large repository.
tutorial.github_and_worktree_body:
List PRs and Issues through gh and read the changes as an inline diff (no extra authentication setup needed).
⚡ Start on an Issue chains together creating a dedicated worktree, adding it to the workspace, and launching an agent.
tutorial.gutter_body:
To the left of the line numbers, git additions / changes and language-server warnings / errors appear side by side.
Even while you are typing, you can see the uncommitted diff.
tutorial.image_pdf_preview_body:
png/jpg/gif/webp/ico open in the image viewer (⌘scroll to zoom 0.05×-32×).
PDFs expand into read-only text with page separators.
Markdown / HTML can be switched to a rendered view.
tutorial.inline_comments_body:
In a diff tab, click a line to write a comment right there. You can also track resolved / unresolved.
All unresolved comments become a single prompt you can hand straight to an agent.
tutorial.install_zero_conflict_and_selfc: Install zero-conflict into this repository and run a self-check right away
tutorial.install_zero_conflict_gate: Place the Zero-Conflict Gate in This Repository
tutorial.intro_body:
We'll walk through the instruments of this cockpit, lighting up where each one lives.
It takes about 2 minutes. You can stop any time with Skip.
tutorial.judge_by_reported_state: Judge by the State the Agent Reports, Not by Reading the Screen
tutorial.jump_to_line_symbol_definition: Jump to a Line, Symbol or Definition
tutorial.jump_to_line_symbol_definition_:
Jump by line and column, from the symbol list, to a definition, or to the matching bracket.
Every one of them is a single keystroke away.
tutorial.jump_to_onscreen_word: Jump to Any Word on Screen in Two Keystrokes
tutorial.launch_bar_body:
Line up to 9 of your most-used agents and launch them by pressing their number.
They come from presets in config.toml, so you can swap in as many as you like.
tutorial.launch_permissions_cockpit_boar: Launch, Permissions, Cockpit, Board, Race, Approvals
tutorial.markdown_images_pdf_wrap: Markdown / HTML, Images, PDF, Wrapping and Whitespace
tutorial.mcp_and_skills_body:
Register MCP servers and manage Skills and slash commands right from the UI.
Every tool you have added to your agents is listed here.
tutorial.merge_train_and_append_automerg: Merge Train and Auto-Merge for Appends
tutorial.merge_train_fewer_stops:
Because the order is fixed and branches go through one at a time, you get stopped less often.
Append-only changes, such as adding a line to a list, are never allowed to collide in the first place.
tutorial.mesh_and_spec_body:
Here you watch the traffic between parallel agents and the automatic release of assignments whose owner died.
Spec tracks drift and staleness between the specification and the implementation.
tutorial.move_between_tabs_by_keyboard:
Going to the next tab, switching in most-recently-used order, and reopening a closed tab are all within reach of the keyboard.
The same keys work even when the editor is split.
tutorial.multi_caret_next_occurrence:
Adding the next occurrence of the selected word keeps adding carets, so you can type into all of them at once.
Use it when you want to fix the same name everywhere in one go.
tutorial.narrow_to_stale_specs: Narrow the view down to stale specs only
tutorial.navigate_diffs_body:
Jump to the next / previous change, or the next / previous changed file, with keystrokes alone.
Even in a large PR you never have to hunt for the scroll position.
tutorial.no_key_assigned: {label} has no keystroke assigned (assign one in ⚙ Settings → Keybindings)
tutorial.notifications_body:
When approval is needed, you can hit ✔Approve / ✖Deny from the popup, the sound cue, or the bubble.
Set webhook_url and it also reaches you on the go via ntfy / Slack / Discord.
Four looks and three sizes; clicking opens the Cockpit.
tutorial.open_chapters_and_index: Opens chapter-by-chapter reading and the index of every feature
tutorial.ownership_ledger: A Ledger That Never Hands the Same File or Line Range to Two Agents
tutorial.ownership_split_proof_train_rad: Ownership, Assignment Splitting, One-Shot Merge Proof, Train, Radar
tutorial.phone_remote_via_qr:
📱 Just scan the QR code and a phone on the same Wi-Fi becomes a remote control (approvals, instructions, even editing).
Authentication is a random token generated at every launch, and it only reaches inside your LAN.
On Windows you can create the inbound rule from the same screen.
tutorial.preview_body:
Switch to a rendered view of exactly what you are editing.
Tables, code blocks and links all come out readable.
tutorial.problems_panel_body:
Open all diagnostics together and step to the next / previous problem in order.
Build task results collect here too.
tutorial.prove_one_shot_merge: Look Only at the Diffs Actually Written and Declare the Merge Lands in One Shot
tutorial.read_diff_and_diagnostics_in_gu: Read Diffs and Diagnostics in the Gutter
tutorial.real_pty_body:
It is a real PTY, so IME input and colors just work.
Drag and drop a file, or paste a clipboard image with ⌘V, and an @path is inserted (it is not sent).
tutorial.real_pty_terminals_voice: A Real PTY, Multiple Terminals, Voice Input
tutorial.rebind_shortcuts_body:
Change assignments one row at a time in Settings, and restore a default right there.
Only the rows you changed are written back to config.toml.
tutorial.run_branches_one_at_a_time: Fix the order and run them one at a time — you get stopped less often
tutorial.screen_not_open: (This screen is not open right now. Moving on shortly)
tutorial.search_and_replace_body:
Search the whole workspace with regular expressions, glob filters and bulk replace.
If you have several folders open, it spans every root.
tutorial.see_parallel_agent_traffic: See All Parallel Agent Traffic on One Screen
tutorial.semantic_conflict_body:
It finds changes that clash even though the files are different.
Conflicts on nearby lines are surfaced early by comparing the worktrees while they run.
tutorial.semantic_conflicts_and_radar: Semantic Conflicts and the Conflict Radar
tutorial.session_history_body:
Conversation history is kept per folder, so reopening restores the previous tabs together with their scrollback.
claude gets --continue and codex gets resume --last automatically, so the CLI-side conversation resumes too.
tutorial.shift_to_free_line_ranges: Instead of Refusing, Shift to a Free Line Range and Hand It Out Again
tutorial.show_feature_now: Opens this feature right now to show you
tutorial.show_nearby_line_conflicts_earl: Surface Nearby-Line Conflicts Between Parallel Worktrees While They Run
tutorial.sidebar_agent_list_body:
One vertical column gathers running sessions, past sessions and new launches.
Pick one with ↑↓ and its terminal appears on the right (below, on a narrow screen).
Stacked mode shows several sessions one above another at the same time.
tutorial.split_panes_body:
Split to the right or downward and jump between panes by their number.
Handy when you want the diff and the implementation side by side.
tutorial.tabs_lines_carets_splits_viewer: Tabs, Line Editing, Multiple Carets, Splits, Viewers
tutorial.themes_and_keybindings_body:
7 dark and 4 light themes are built in, and you can load VS Code compatible theme JSON as-is.
Every shortcut can be replaced under [keybindings] in config.toml.
tutorial.themes_shortcuts_zoom_plugins_e: Themes, Shortcuts, Zoom, Plugins, External Control
tutorial.three_approval_modes_one_click:
🛡Approval / ⚡Full auto / 👾Agent-first — switch between the three modes with one click, and push the change to running sessions all at once.
Automatic answers to interactive prompts are a separate switch, "⚡ Auto YES", and it is off by default.
The last YES is always yours.
tutorial.top_toolbar_body:
Cockpit, the board, permission modes, 📱, 🎤 and other frequently used controls line up here.
This is the instrument panel of your cockpit.
tutorial.track_spec_drift: Track Drift and Staleness Between Spec and Implementation
tutorial.unread_rounds_body:
Cycle through only the agents that need your hand.
Agents you want to postpone can be marked unread again and skipped to the next.
tutorial.vertical_agent_list_body:
See the running agents in a vertical list and jump straight to the terminal of the one you pick.
On a narrow screen this gets you there faster.
tutorial.voice_input_keeps_flowing:
🎤 starts it, and what you say keeps flowing into the input box (⏹ stops it).
Enter is never pressed for you, so you read it, fix it, and send it yourself once you are happy.
The destination — 🎯 active or 📣 all agents — can be switched while you are still recording.
tutorial.wrap_and_whitespace_body:
From the View menu (or the command palette): Toggle Word Wrap and Toggle Whitespace.
Spaces show as · and tabs as →.
Defaults live in config.toml; per-project overrides go in .zaivern.toml.
tutorial.zai_cli_body:
zai open / prompt / run / notify let you drive this running editor from outside.
zai status lists the running instances and returns exit code 1 when there are none.
tutorial.zero_conflict_body:
The value of running agents in parallel is cancelled out by the conflict resolution you pay for later.
So assignments are split into disjoint sets before dispatch, ownership of files and line ranges is claimed in a ledger, and only the diffs actually written are examined to declare that the merge will land in one shot.
tutorial.zero_conflict_install_body:
Run the setup and the self-check in one go to see how far you are protected right now.
Every repository is judged under the same conditions, so the result never varies by environment.
tutorial.zero_conflict_never_share_a_lin: Zero Conflict — Never Hand the Same Line to Two Agents
tutorial.zoom_and_fullscreen_body:
Zooming the whole window and zooming just this file work independently.
Switching to full screen leaves everything you have open exactly as it was.
